<!-- Generated by docs-infra Python API -->

```python
place_params(params: Mapping[str, np.ndarray], device: _core.Device) -> dict[str, 'evoxc.Tensor']
```

Part of [`evoxc_hf.pipeline`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/)

Also available as `evoxc_hf.place_params`.

Copy every parameter onto `device` — explicit per-leaf placement.

A non-cpu executable rejects host inputs at its run boundary by design
(`evoxc.DeviceError`), so this is the documented way to prepare weights
for a device-resident run: one explicit `Tensor.to(device)` per leaf, no
hidden move. Use the result as the `params` argument of `run` and
feed each run's outputs back as the next run's inputs (the documented
same-device loop).

Packed weights fit here unchanged, and the supported order is **pack on the
host first, then place the packed tree**: `place_params(packed, device)`
transfers the ~4–8 packed leaves instead of one leaf per weight (~200 for
the 124M models) — the same bytes, a fraction of the per-leaf staging calls.

## Parameters

- `params` · `Mapping[str, np.ndarray]` — canonical flat params mapping (host arrays, e.g.
  `evoxc_hf.load_hf(model_dir).params`) — or, after
  `evoxc_hf.pack_params`, the packed tree.

- `device` · `_core.Device` — the target `evoxc.core.Device` (e.g. `Device("cuda", 0)`).

## Returns

- `dict[str, 'evoxc.Tensor']` — dict[str, evoxc.Tensor]: the same keys, each value a device `Tensor`.

## Raises

- `TypeError` — `device` is not an `evoxc.core.Device`, `params` is
  not a mapping, a key is not a string, or a value is not convertible
  to a numpy array.
